{"concern":"core","designation":"internal","kind":"functional","lineage":"original","name":"A default must not assert what nobody chose","priority":"medium","provenance":"authored","statement":"FOUND BY A DELIBERATE SWEEP, 2026-07-28, asking the question `req:supporting-is-not-conflict` implies but does not answer: what ELSE does the schema claim that no computation checks? The sweep was Anthony's call after the same defect shape appeared six times in three days.

THE MEASURED FINDING. Ten properties are materialised onto every node by the store's schema defaults and appear ZERO times in the entire Rust source — not in a detector, not in a report, not in a test. Measured against reflow2's own 860-node design:

- `Requirement.concern` — `core` on 67 of 67
- `Capability.tier` — `operational` on 84 of 84
- `Component.tier` — `operational` on 53 of 53
- `Capability.is_entry_point` / `is_exit_point` — `false` on 84 of 84
- `Constraint.concern`, `DesignRule.enforced`, `Actor.actor_type`, `EnvironmentRule.mandatory`, `EnvironmentRule.rule_type`, `Flow.tier` — likewise defaulted, likewise unread

Single-valued across the whole design, every one. A property that never varies is not carrying information; it is asserting one.

THE WORST INSTANCE, and the reason this is intent rather than tidiness. `Requirement.concern`'s enum is core / logistics / sustainment / safety / security / cost / schedule / manufacturability / usability / environmental — and the schema's own description says logistics and sustainment are there to carry "the ILS considerations an SME surfaces". That is the systems-engineering angle this project exists to serve, encoded in the schema and then asserted away: every requirement claims `core`, there is NO WRITER for it on the MCP surface (only the `create_node` escape hatch — the same shape as the KPP `objective` finding), and nothing reads it. So "which of these are the safety requirements?" cannot be answered, and the graph does not answer "unknown" — it answers "none".

THE RULE, AND IT IS ALREADY PROVEN HERE. `Interface.medium` defaulting to `REST` was fixed on 2026-07-28 for exactly this reason, and `ver:interface-spec` states the principle in the form it should now generalise: "UNRECORDED FIELDS READ AS `unspecified` NOT `none` — the flattering default would tell a consumer an unspecified contract is open." So: A DEFAULT MAY RECORD ABSENCE; IT MAY NOT RECORD A CHOICE. Where a property has a substantive default nobody selected, the default becomes `unspecified` and silence reads as silence.

WHY IT IS NOT MERELY COSMETIC. `export_surface` publishes a design's boundary to another design; a mirrored surface carrying `tier: operational` and `concern: core` ships assertions nobody made across a seam, which is the same failure `req:publishable-promise` was raised for one layer down. And the moment any future computation DOES read one of these — the SME view `concern` was designed for — it reads a value the schema invented.

THE COUNTERWEIGHT, and it is what stops this being a blanket rewrite: a default that records a genuine absence is CORRECT and must stay. `provenance: authored` and `status: proposed` are real defaults meaning a real thing. The test is whether the default names a CHOICE among alternatives (tier, concern, rule_type) or the ABSENCE of one — only the first kind lies. Changing a default is also not retroactive: nodes written before the change keep the value they were given, so a sweep of existing designs is a separate, deliberate act.

SIBLING FINDINGS FROM THE SAME SWEEP, recorded here rather than lost. (1) Fifteen properties are WRITTEN and never consulted — the sharpest is `DriftEvent.severity`, written from `kind.severity()` at three call sites while ranking independently re-derives it via `severity_rank(kind)`, so the stored copy can silently diverge from the mapping that actually governs; also `DesignEpoch.sequence`, which COORD entries quote as meaningful ("epoch:v0180 at sequence 210") and nothing orders by. (2) `req:supporting-is-not-conflict` is an instance of ITSELF: it carries `concern: core`, one of the properties nothing reads.","status":"proposed"}
